title: Mechanical Duck Launcher Puzzle
description: A physics-inspired puzzle where the player configures a gear-driven catapult to launch rubber ducks into shader ball targets. Players adjust gear ratios, launch angle, and power to conserve momentum across multiple shots, with full undo/redo support for each configuration step.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load ShaderBall.glb, gears.glb, and Duck.glb. Scene setup: place a ground plane with grid texture. Position the gears model on the left as a mechanical launcher mechanism. Place 3 ShaderBall models at varying distances (10, 18, 27 units) and heights (0, 3, 6 units) on the right side as targets, each glowing with a distinct emissive color (red, green, blue). The Duck is the projectile, sitting on the launcher. Camera: perspective at (0,12,-20) looking at scene center. Lighting: ambient light plus two directional lights with shadows enabled on the ground plane. Interactions (10-14 steps total): 1) Click gears to cycle through 3 gear ratios (1x, 2x, 3x) which visually spin the gears at different speeds and set a power multiplier. 2) Use a draggable HTML slider (0-90 degrees) to set launch angle, visually tilting the gear assembly. 3) Use a second slider to set lateral aim (-30 to 30 degrees). 4) Press SPACE to launch the duck along a parabolic arc using the configured parameters. The duck follows projectile motion where total energy is conserved: kinetic energy converts to potential energy at peak. 5) On hit, the ShaderBall shatters into particles and score increases by distance multiplied by gear ratio. On miss, the duck splashes on the ground. 6) After each shot, a new duck loads automatically. 7) Implement full undo (Ctrl+Z) and redo (Ctrl+Y) for all configuration changes and launches, restoring target states and score. Display an HUD showing current gear ratio, angle, aim, score, shots taken, and undo/redo stack depth. The player must hit all 3 targets to win. Animate gear teeth rotating continuously based on selected ratio. Add a trail particle effect behind the flying duck using a simple point cloud.
